parsed_profile_json.title: HEAVY-DUTY GAS TURBINE SHIM MIGRATION AND LOSS
parsed_profile_json.reason_for_revision: Revised to add additional gas turbine classes and to update recommendations.
parsed_profile_json.purpose: To inform users of the need to monitor the condition of compressor shims and corrective actions necessary to mitigate the risks of migrating shims.
parsed_profile_json.compliance_category_text: Maintenance - Identifies maintenance guidelines or best practices for reliable equipment operation.
parsed_profile_json.coarse_outage_type: Scheduled Component Part Repair or Replacement
scope_of_work: Continue normal borescope and visual inspections per GER 3620, noting the condition of all shims.

Implement shim attachment modification (drive pins to align and mechanically attach each shim to an adjacent stator base/segment) during scheduled outages in which the compressor casing has been removed (next major inspection interval or next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed).
service_recommendation_line_items: Perform borescope and visual inspections per GER 3620; document shim condition and report any shim anomalies to local GE Service Manager or Contract Performance Manager.
If evidence of shim migration is found, apply corrective action based on stage, protrusion into airflow, and migration rate; perform follow-up inspections as needed to evaluate migration rate.

If protruding shims are accessible: remove the shim if it can be done without risk of damaging neighboring blades/vanes; operate with shim removed until next planned casing removal outage for re-shimming.
If removal is difficult and accessible: grind the shim flush with the flow path without risk of damaging neighboring blades/vanes; after grinding, inspect for further movement after 25 starts.
Disposition front-end shims with GREATER than 50% height protrusion prior to restart of the unit.

Plan and implement GE shim pinning modification (preferred solution) at next major inspection (MI) interval or next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed; order shim pinning modification kit and allow 10 weeks for parts delivery.
Use replacement shims of no less than 80 mils thickness for robust retention.
parsed_profile_json.maintenance_trigger_text: Borescope inspections should be completed annually and at regular maintenance outages (CI & HGPI) as outlined in GER3620. Shim modification recommended at the next major inspection (MI) interval or the next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed. Front-end shims with GREATER than 50% height protrusion require disposition prior to restart. After grinding accessible shims flush, inspect for further movement after 25 starts.
recommended_interval_or_trigger: Complete borescope inspections annually and at regular maintenance outages (CI & HGPI) as outlined in GER3620.
Implement shim modification at the next major inspection (MI) interval or the next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed.
After grinding accessible shims flush with the flow path, inspect for further movement after 25 starts.
Front-end shims with GREATER than 50% height protrusion require disposition prior to restart of the unit.
Aft stage shim migration can typically be addressed at the scheduled major inspection interval.
parsed_profile_json.usage_counter_requirements_text: If the shim is accessible for grinding, it is recommended to do so and then inspect for further movement after 25 starts.
parsed_profile_json.frame_or_model_applicability_text: All B, C, E, F, and H-Class gas turbines.
parsed_profile_json.hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Compressor stator shims retained via two retention hooks; GE shim attachment modification uses drive pins to align and mechanically attach each shim to an adjacent stator base/segment (available for all compressor stages). Replacement shims should be of no less than 80 mils thickness.
parsed_profile_json.exclusions_or_non_applicable_conditions_: Stages 0-4 on the 7H machine, 1-4 on the 9H machine, and 1-2 on the 6C machine do not have shims (Variable Guide Vanes (VGV) and do not use shims). It is normal for some stages to be without shims; due to manufacturing variation, shims may not be necessary for every stage.
parsed_profile_json.prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: Implementation of the shim modification will be carried out during scheduled outages in which the compressor casing has been removed; recommended at next MI interval or next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed.
parsed_profile_json.sbom_trigger_reason: TIL references a configuration-dependent hardware enhancement (shim pinning modification kit with shims and pins) that requires installed-configuration verification and parts ordering.

parts_referenced.context: Shim pinning modification kit (kit containing the necessary shims and pins to complete the job) for shim attachment modification using drive pins.
Replacement shims (recommended thickness no less than 80 mils) for robust retention.

reference_documents.context: Normal borescope and visual inspections and inspection/outage cadence (CI & HGPI) are referenced as outlined in GER3620.

configuration_variables: Gas turbine class/frame (B, C, E, F, H; including 9E, 7H, 9H, 6C stage differences)
Compressor stage location (front-end vs aft stages; specific stages with/without shims)
Shim protrusion amount into airflow (LESS than 50% vs GREATER than 50% height protrusion)
Shim accessibility for removal or grinding
Migration rate (follow-up inspections may be necessary to evaluate rate)
parsed_profile_json.configuration_summary: Recommendations vary by turbine class and compressor stage (including stages that do not use shims on certain H and C machines), and by shim condition (protrusion percentage, accessibility, and migration rate). Shim pinning modification is applicable to all compressor stages and recommended at MI or rotor-exposed compressor maintenance outage.
severity_signals: Evidence of shim migration (movement of shims out of stator grooves and into the flow path).
Front-end shims with GREATER than 50% height protrusion.
Continued movement of front-end shims (elevates risk).
failure_consequences: Shim liberation could lead to compressor damage.
Flow disturbances from protruding shims can further accelerate shim migration.
parsed_profile_json.risk_summary: Shim migration poses a risk of shim liberation leading to compressor damage; risk is greatest for front stages due to shim size and number of stages that could be impacted. Front-end shims with >50% protrusion require disposition prior to restart; aft stage migration is considered low-risk and typically addressed at major inspection.

source_snippets.snippet: To inform users of the need to monitor the condition of compressor shims and corrective actions necessary to mitigate the risks of migrating shims.
All B, C, E, F, and H-Class gas turbines
Shim migration poses a risk of shim liberation, which could lead to compressor damage.
Operators should continue normal borescope and visual inspections per GER 3620, noting the condition of all shims.

Remove the shim, if it can be done without risk of damaging neighboring blades/vanes. Operating with a shim removed is acceptable until the next planned casing removal outage, at which time re-shimming can be performed.
Grind the shim flush with the flow path.
If the shim is accessible for grinding, it is recommended to do so and then inspect for further movement after 25 starts.
Front-end shims with GREATER than 50% height protrusion pose a greater risk for liberation, regardless of their history, and require disposition prior to restart of the unit.

For all B, C, E, F, and H-Class gas turbines, GE recommends the shim modification be implemented at the next major inspection (MI) interval or the next compressor maintenance outage in which the rotor is exposed.
A kit containing the necessary shims and pins to complete the job must be ordered for the modification.
Borescope inspections, requiring approximately 8-12 hours to complete, should be completed annually and at regular maintenance outages (CI & HGPI) as outlined in GER3620.
